questions.prompt: Organic chemistry is the study of which kind of compounds?
questions.explanation: Organic chemistry is the study of carbon-based compounds, which are fundamental to life.

questions.prompt: Which of these fields depends on knowing the structures and reactions of organic molecules?
questions.explanation: Understanding organic molecules is crucial for medicine, materials science and environmental science.

options: Medicine, materials science and environmental science

questions.prompt: A hydrocarbon contains which elements only?
questions.explanation: A hydrocarbon is a compound that contains carbon and hydrogen only.

questions.prompt: Which three families of hydrocarbons are studied in this unit?
questions.explanation: The hydrocarbon families are alkanes (C–C single bonds), alkenes (C=C) and alkynes (C≡C).

questions.prompt: What is a functional group?
questions.explanation: All compounds with the same functional group belong to the same class.

options: The total number of hydrogen atoms in a molecule
A group of students studying chemistry
A chain of carbon atoms only
An atom or group of atoms that classifies an organic compound into a class

questions.prompt: Which functional group is present in alcohols?
questions.explanation: Alcohols contain the hydroxyl group –OH.

questions.prompt: Which functional group is present in carboxylic acids?
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids contain the carboxyl group –COOH.

questions.prompt: Which functional group is present in esters?
questions.explanation: Esters have the ester group –COO– between two carbon groups (RCOOR′).

questions.prompt: What is the general formula of an ester?
questions.explanation: An ester has the general formula RCOOR′; R and R′ may be the same or different.

questions.prompt: What is the general formula of a carboxylic acid?
questions.explanation: A carboxylic acid is written RCOOH.

questions.prompt: What does a structural formula show?
questions.explanation: A structural formula shows how the atoms are joined up or arranged in a molecule or compound.

options: How the different atoms are joined up or arranged in a molecule
Only the mass of a molecule
Only the colour of a compound
Only the number of atoms in a molecule

questions.prompt: In how many ways can a structural formula be drawn in this chapter?
questions.explanation: The two ways are the displayed formula and the condensed (normal) structural formula.

questions.prompt: In a displayed formula, how are bonds shown?
questions.explanation: A displayed formula shows all the bonds between the atoms as individual lines.

options: Every bond as an individual line

questions.prompt: A double bond in a displayed formula is drawn as
questions.explanation: One line = single bond, two lines = double bond, three lines = triple bond.

questions.prompt: A triple bond in a displayed formula is drawn as
questions.explanation: Three lines show a triple bond (C≡C).

questions.prompt: What is the main drawback of a displayed formula?
questions.explanation: Displayed formulae give the most information but are large and slow to draw.

options: It is very large and time-consuming to draw
It hides how the atoms are joined

questions.prompt: A displayed formula is always drawn with the molecule
questions.explanation: The molecule is straightened out and flattened to show exactly how all the atoms are joined.

options: Written in one line of text
Shown only as a three-dimensional model

questions.prompt: A condensed (normal) structural formula
questions.explanation: In a condensed formula atoms attached to the same carbon are grouped, e.g. CH₃CH₃.

options: Shows every bond as a separate line
Omits some or all bonds and groups atoms joined to the same carbon
Shows only the name of the compound
Shows only the number of carbon atoms

questions.prompt: What is the –CH₃ group called?
questions.explanation: –CH₃ is the methyl group and –CH₂– is the methylene group.

questions.prompt: What is the –CH₂– group called?
questions.explanation: –CH₂– is the methylene group.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly compares displayed and condensed formulae?
questions.explanation: Displayed formulae give a clear view of connections; condensed formulae are more concise.

options: Both are identical in every way
Condensed formulae show every bond as a line
Condensed formulae are more concise; displayed formulae show how the atoms are connected
Displayed formulae are always shorter than condensed formulae

questions.prompt: How many bonds does each carbon atom form in organic compounds?
questions.explanation: Every carbon atom forms four bonds.

questions.prompt: How many bonds does a hydrogen atom form?
questions.explanation: In structural formulae C = 4 lines, O = 2 lines and H = 1 line.

questions.prompt: How many bonds does an oxygen atom form in alcohols and acids?
questions.explanation: Oxygen forms two bonds (for example C–O–H in an alcohol).

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are attached directly to carbon 1 of but-1-ene? (number the chain as in the name)
questions.explanation: Every carbon has four bonds. In but-1-ene (CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃) carbon 1 has 2 H.

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are attached directly to carbon 2 of pentane? (number the chain as in the name)
questions.explanation: Every carbon has four bonds. In pentane (CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃) carbon 2 has 2 H.

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are attached directly to carbon 2 of but-1-yne? (number the chain as in the name)
questions.explanation: Every carbon has four bonds. In but-1-yne (CH≡CCH₂CH₃) carbon 2 has 0 H.

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are attached directly to carbon 2 of but-2-ene? (number the chain as in the name)
questions.explanation: Every carbon has four bonds. In but-2-ene (CH₃CH=CHCH₃) carbon 2 has 1 H.

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are attached directly to carbon 1 of pentan-2-ol? (number the chain as in the name)
questions.explanation: Every carbon has four bonds. In pentan-2-ol (CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₂CH₃) carbon 1 has 3 H.

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are attached directly to carbon 1 of but-2-ene? (number the chain as in the name)
questions.explanation: Every carbon has four bonds. In but-2-ene (CH₃CH=CHCH₃) carbon 1 has 3 H.

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are attached directly to carbon 1 of propane? (number the chain as in the name)
questions.explanation: Every carbon has four bonds. In propane (CH₃CH₂CH₃) carbon 1 has 3 H.

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are attached directly to carbon 4 of pent-1-ene? (number the chain as in the name)
questions.explanation: Every carbon has four bonds. In pent-1-ene (CH₂=CHCH₂CH₂CH₃) carbon 4 has 2 H.

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are attached directly to carbon 1 of propan-1-ol? (number the chain as in the name)
questions.explanation: Every carbon has four bonds. In propan-1-ol (CH₃CH₂CH₂OH) carbon 1 has 2 H.

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are attached directly to carbon 2 of butane? (number the chain as in the name)
questions.explanation: Every carbon has four bonds. In butane (CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃) carbon 2 has 2 H.

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are attached directly to carbon 2 of propan-1-ol? (number the chain as in the name)
questions.explanation: Every carbon has four bonds. In propan-1-ol (CH₃CH₂CH₂OH) carbon 2 has 2 H.

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are attached directly to carbon 4 of but-1-ene? (number the chain as in the name)
questions.explanation: Every carbon has four bonds. In but-1-ene (CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃) carbon 4 has 3 H.

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are attached directly to carbon 2 of but-2-yne? (number the chain as in the name)
questions.explanation: Every carbon has four bonds. In but-2-yne (CH₃C≡CCH₃) carbon 2 has 0 H.

questions.prompt: The stems for one, two, three and four carbon atoms are
questions.explanation: Remember “Mice Eat Peanut Butter” = meth, eth, prop, but.

questions.prompt: Which stem means five carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: Pentagon has 5 sides, so pent = 5.

questions.prompt: Which stem means six carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: Hexagon has 6 sides, so hex = 6.

questions.prompt: Which stem means seven carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: Heptagon has 7 sides, so hept = 7.

questions.prompt: Which stem means eight carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: Octagon has 8 sides, so oct = 8.

questions.prompt: Which stem means nine carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: Nonagon has 9 sides, so non = 9.

questions.prompt: Which stem means ten carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: Decagon has 10 sides, so dec = 10.

questions.prompt: How many carbon atoms does the stem “oct” represent?
questions.explanation: oct = 8 carbon atoms (octane).

questions.prompt: The suffix used for alkanes is
questions.explanation: Alkane = single bonds only = -ane.

questions.prompt: The suffix used for alkenes is
questions.explanation: Alkene = C=C = -ene.

questions.prompt: The suffix used for alkynes is
questions.explanation: Alkyne = C≡C = -yne.

questions.prompt: The suffix used for alcohols is
questions.explanation: The final “e” of the alkane name is replaced by “ol”.

questions.prompt: The suffix used for carboxylic acids is
questions.explanation: The final “e” of the alkane name is replaced by “oic acid”.

questions.prompt: Esters have names of the form
questions.explanation: First word from the alcohol (-yl), second word from the acid (-oate).

questions.prompt: What is the trick “a – e – y = 1 – 2 – 3”?
questions.explanation: a – e – y follows the alphabet, like 1 – 2 – 3 bonds. -ane = single, -ene = double, -yne = triple.

options: The order of the vowels in the alphabet only
The letters a, e, y in -ane, -ene, -yne match single, double and triple bonds
The number of hydrogens in each alkane
The number of carbons in methane, ethane and propane

questions.prompt: What does IUPAC stand for?
questions.explanation: IUPAC gives a standard set of rules for naming compounds.

options: International Union of Pure and Atomic Chemistry
International Union of Physical and Applied Chemistry
Indian Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry
International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry

questions.prompt: Why is the IUPAC naming system used?
questions.explanation: IUPAC names are based on structure and avoid the confusion caused by common names.

options: It gives each compound a different common name in each country
It gives standard rules so compounds can be identified regardless of language or region
It names compounds only by their colour
It makes every compound name shorter than one word

questions.prompt: The two parts of every IUPAC organic name are the
questions.explanation: The stem shows the number of carbons; the suffix shows the family.

questions.prompt: The stem of an organic name tells you
questions.explanation: meth = 1, eth = 2, prop = 3, but = 4, and so on.

options: The number of carbon atoms in the longest chain

questions.prompt: The suffix (ending) of an organic name tells you
questions.explanation: The suffix is the ending of the name and is placed after the stem.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the alkane with four carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: but + ane = butane, CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ (C₄H₁₀).

questions.prompt: Meth + ane gives
questions.explanation: The stem meth means one carbon and -ane means alkane.

questions.prompt: Alkanes are hydrocarbons in which all the carbon atoms are joined by
questions.explanation: All C–C bonds in an alkane are single bonds.

questions.prompt: Which is the simplest alkane?
questions.explanation: Methane (one carbon) is the simplest alkane.

questions.prompt: What is the general formula of the alkanes?
questions.explanation: Butane C₄H₁₀ has 2 × 4 + 2 = 10 hydrogen atoms.

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are on each END carbon of an unbranched alkane?
questions.explanation: End carbons carry three H; middle carbons carry two H.

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are on each MIDDLE carbon of an unbranched alkane?
questions.explanation: A middle carbon has two C–C bonds and two C–H bonds.

questions.prompt: How many C–C and C–H bonds are in the displayed formula of propane?
questions.explanation: Propane has 2 C–C bonds and 8 C–H bonds (ten bonds in all).

questions.prompt: Which condensed formula can also be written CH₃(CH₂)₃CH₃?
questions.explanation: CH₃(CH₂)₃CH₃ means CH₃, three CH₂ groups, then CH₃: five carbons, so pentane.

questions.prompt: How is CH₃(CH₂)₆CH₃ named?
questions.explanation: CH₃ + six CH₂ + CH₃ = eight carbons, so octane (C₈H₁₈).

questions.prompt: How is CH₃(CH₂)₈CH₃ named?
questions.explanation: CH₃ + eight CH₂ + CH₃ = ten carbons, so decane (C₁₀H₂₂).

questions.prompt: Using CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, how many hydrogen atoms are in the alkane with 9 carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: 2 × 9 + 2 = 20 hydrogen atoms: C₉H₂₀.

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are present in one molecule of heptane?
questions.explanation: Heptane: hept = 7 carbons and -ane = only single bonds, so CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ (C₇H₁₆).

questions.prompt: To which family does the compound CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ belong?
questions.explanation: CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ is an alkane: it has only single bonds between carbon atoms.

questions.prompt: Which compound has the molecular formula C₆H₁₄?
questions.explanation: Hexane: hex = 6 carbons and -ane = only single bonds, so CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ (C₆H₁₄).

questions.prompt: Using CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, how many hydrogen atoms are in the alkane with 10 carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: 2 × 10 + 2 = 22 hydrogen atoms: C₁₀H₂₂.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct name of the compound with the condensed formula CH₃CH₂CH₃?
questions.explanation: Propane: prop = 3 carbons and -ane = only single bonds, so CH₃CH₂CH₃ (C₃H₈).

questions.prompt: What is the condensed structural formula of ethane?
questions.explanation: Ethane: eth = 2 carbons and -ane = only single bonds, so CH₃CH₃ (C₂H₆).

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are present in one molecule of decane?
questions.explanation: Decane: dec = 10 carbons and -ane = only single bonds, so CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ (C₁₀H₂₂).

questions.prompt: To which family does the compound CH₄ belong?
questions.explanation: CH₄ is an alkane: it has only single bonds between carbon atoms.

questions.prompt: What is the condensed structural formula of propane?
questions.explanation: Propane: prop = 3 carbons and -ane = only single bonds, so CH₃CH₂CH₃ (C₃H₈).

questions.prompt: How many atoms in total are present in one molecule of methane?
questions.explanation: Methane is CH₄: 1 C + 4 H = 5 atoms.

questions.prompt: Which general formula does nonane fit?
questions.explanation: Nonane is an alkane, so it fits CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

questions.prompt: What is the molecular formula of ethane?
questions.explanation: Ethane: eth = 2 carbons and -ane = only single bonds, so CH₃CH₃ (C₂H₆).

questions.prompt: Which is the correct name of the compound with the condensed formula CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃?
questions.explanation: Heptane: hept = 7 carbons and -ane = only single bonds, so CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ (C₇H₁₆).

questions.prompt: Which compound has the molecular formula C₂H₆?
questions.explanation: Ethane: eth = 2 carbons and -ane = only single bonds, so CH₃CH₃ (C₂H₆).

questions.prompt: Which compound has the molecular formula C₇H₁₆?
questions.explanation: Heptane: hept = 7 carbons and -ane = only single bonds, so CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ (C₇H₁₆).

questions.prompt: Which alkane has the molecular formula C₉H₂₀?
questions.explanation: Nonane has 9 carbons (non) and 20 hydrogens.

questions.prompt: Which compound has the molecular formula C₈H₁₈?
questions.explanation: Octane: oct = 8 carbons and -ane = only single bonds, so CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ (C₈H₁₈).

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are present in one molecule of butane?
questions.explanation: Butane: but = 4 carbons and -ane = only single bonds, so CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ (C₄H₁₀).

questions.prompt: How many atoms in total are present in one molecule of octane?
questions.explanation: Octane is C₈H₁₈: 8 C + 18 H = 26 atoms.

questions.prompt: Which general formula does butane fit?
questions.explanation: Butane is an alkane, so it fits CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are present in one molecule of pentane?
questions.explanation: Pentane: pent = 5 carbons and -ane = only single bonds, so CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ (C₅H₁₂).

questions.prompt: Which general formula does heptane fit?
questions.explanation: Heptane is an alkane, so it fits CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

questions.prompt: How many carbon atoms are present in one molecule of pentane?
questions.explanation: Pentane: pent = 5 carbons and -ane = only single bonds, so CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ (C₅H₁₂).

questions.prompt: Using CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, how many hydrogen atoms are in the alkane with 6 carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: 2 × 6 + 2 = 14 hydrogen atoms: C₆H₁₄.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct name of the compound with the condensed formula CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃?
questions.explanation: Decane: dec = 10 carbons and -ane = only single bonds, so CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ (C₁₀H₂₂).

questions.prompt: How many carbon atoms are present in one molecule of decane?
questions.explanation: Decane: dec = 10 carbons and -ane = only single bonds, so CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ (C₁₀H₂₂).

questions.prompt: Which general formula does methane fit?
questions.explanation: Methane is an alkane, so it fits CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

questions.prompt: Which alkane has the molecular formula C₅H₁₂?
questions.explanation: Pentane has 5 carbons (pent) and 12 hydrogens.

questions.prompt: Why do we write numbers in the names but-1-ene and but-2-ene?
questions.explanation: The number of the carbon where the double bond starts is written in the name.

options: To show how many hydrogen atoms there are
The position of the double bond must be shown in larger chains
To show how many carbon atoms there are
To show the number of double bonds only

questions.prompt: Alkenes are hydrocarbons that contain
questions.explanation: Alkenes contain at least one C=C double bond.

options: At least one carbon–carbon double bond
At least one carbon–carbon triple bond

questions.prompt: What is the general formula of the alkenes?
questions.explanation: Ethene C₂H₄, propene C₃H₆, butene C₄H₈ all fit CₙH₂ₙ.

questions.prompt: How is a carbon–carbon double bond formed?
questions.explanation: A double covalent bond is two shared pairs of electrons.

options: One carbon atom gives two electrons to the other
Two carbon atoms share one pair of electrons
Two carbon atoms share three pairs of electrons
Two carbon atoms share two pairs of electrons

questions.prompt: With how many OTHER atoms does a doubly bonded carbon form single bonds?
questions.explanation: A doubly bonded carbon uses two of its four bonds for C=C and forms single bonds with two other atoms.

questions.prompt: Which is the simplest alkene?
questions.explanation: A double bond needs two carbons, so ethene is the simplest alkene (there is no “methene”).

questions.prompt: Between which carbon atoms is the double bond in but-1-ene?
questions.explanation: In but-1-ene the double bond starts on carbon 1: CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃.

questions.prompt: Between which carbon atoms is the double bond in but-2-ene?
questions.explanation: In but-2-ene the double bond starts on carbon 2: CH₃CH=CHCH₃.

questions.prompt: But-1-ene and but-2-ene are
questions.explanation: The double bond is in a different place, so they are different compounds with the same molecular formula.

options: Different compounds with the same molecular formula C₄H₈
The same compound with two names

questions.prompt: Why is propene NOT written as CH₃CH₂=CH₂?
questions.explanation: CH₂= would give the middle carbon 1 + 2 + 2 = five bonds. The correct formula is CH₃CH=CH₂.

options: Hydrogen cannot be written after carbon
The middle carbon would have five bonds
The formula would have too few carbon atoms

questions.prompt: Which functional group or bond type characterises but-2-ene?
questions.explanation: But-2-ene is an alkene: it has a C=C double bond.

questions.prompt: To which family does the compound CH₃CH₂CH=CHCH₂CH₃ belong?
questions.explanation: CH₃CH₂CH=CHCH₂CH₃ is an alkene: it has a C=C double bond.

questions.prompt: How many carbon atoms are present in one molecule of pent-1-ene?
questions.explanation: Pent-1-ene: pent- = 5 carbons and -1-ene = a C=C double bond starting on C-1, so CH₂=CHCH₂CH₂CH₃ (C₅H₁₀).

questions.prompt: What is the condensed structural formula of hex-3-ene?
questions.explanation: Hex-3-ene: hex- = 6 carbons and -3-ene = a C=C double bond starting on C-3, so CH₃CH₂CH=CHCH₂CH₃ (C₆H₁₂).

questions.prompt: Which is the correct name of the compound with the condensed formula CH₃CH=CHCH₂CH₂CH₃?
questions.explanation: Hex-2-ene: hex- = 6 carbons and -2-ene = a C=C double bond starting on C-2, so CH₃CH=CHCH₂CH₂CH₃ (C₆H₁₂).

questions.prompt: What is the condensed structural formula of propene?
questions.explanation: Propene: prop = 3 carbons and -ene = a C=C double bond, so CH₃CH=CH₂ (C₃H₆).

questions.prompt: Which is the correct name of the compound with the condensed formula CH₃CH₂CH=CHCH₂CH₃?
questions.explanation: Hex-3-ene: hex- = 6 carbons and -3-ene = a C=C double bond starting on C-3, so CH₃CH₂CH=CHCH₂CH₃ (C₆H₁₂).

questions.prompt: What is the condensed structural formula of but-1-ene?
questions.explanation: But-1-ene: but- = 4 carbons and -1-ene = a C=C double bond starting on C-1, so CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃ (C₄H₈).

questions.prompt: How many carbon atoms are present in one molecule of hex-2-ene?
questions.explanation: Hex-2-ene: hex- = 6 carbons and -2-ene = a C=C double bond starting on C-2, so CH₃CH=CHCH₂CH₂CH₃ (C₆H₁₂).

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are present in one molecule of hex-3-ene?
questions.explanation: Hex-3-ene: hex- = 6 carbons and -3-ene = a C=C double bond starting on C-3, so CH₃CH₂CH=CHCH₂CH₃ (C₆H₁₂).

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are present in one molecule of ethene?
questions.explanation: Ethene: eth = 2 carbons and -ene = a C=C double bond, so CH₂=CH₂ (C₂H₄).

questions.prompt: What is the condensed structural formula of pent-2-ene?
questions.explanation: Pent-2-ene: pent- = 5 carbons and -2-ene = a C=C double bond starting on C-2, so CH₃CH=CHCH₂CH₃ (C₅H₁₀).

questions.prompt: What is the condensed structural formula of pent-1-ene?
questions.explanation: Pent-1-ene: pent- = 5 carbons and -1-ene = a C=C double bond starting on C-1, so CH₂=CHCH₂CH₂CH₃ (C₅H₁₀).

questions.prompt: Which general formula does hex-3-ene fit?
questions.explanation: Hex-3-ene is an alkene, so it fits CₙH₂ₙ.

questions.prompt: Which functional group or bond type characterises hex-1-ene?
questions.explanation: Hex-1-ene is an alkene: it has a C=C double bond.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct name of the compound with the condensed formula CH₃CH=CHCH₃?
questions.explanation: But-2-ene: but- = 4 carbons and -2-ene = a C=C double bond starting on C-2, so CH₃CH=CHCH₃ (C₄H₈).

questions.prompt: To which family does the compound CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃ belong?
questions.explanation: CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃ is an alkene: it has a C=C double bond.

questions.prompt: Which is the simplest alkyne?
questions.explanation: A triple bond needs two carbons, so ethyne is the simplest alkyne.

questions.prompt: The compound CH₃C≡CH is called
questions.explanation: Three carbons (prop) with a triple bond (-yne).

questions.prompt: Alkynes are hydrocarbons that contain
questions.explanation: Alkynes have at least one C≡C triple bond.

options: At least one carbon–carbon triple bond
At least one carbon–carbon double bond

questions.prompt: What is the general formula of alkynes with one triple bond?
questions.explanation: Ethyne C₂H₂, propyne C₃H₄, butyne C₄H₆ all fit CₙH₂ₙ₋₂.

questions.prompt: What is the other name of ethyne?
questions.explanation: Ethyne is also called acetylene, H–C≡C–H.

questions.prompt: How many pairs of electrons are shared in a carbon–carbon triple bond?
questions.explanation: A triple bond is three shared pairs of electrons.

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms does each carbon of ethyne carry?
questions.explanation: Each carbon has three bonds in the triple bond plus one bond to hydrogen = four.

questions.prompt: Why is CH₂≡CCH₂CH₃ a wrong formula for but-1-yne?
questions.explanation: A carbon at the end of a triple bond has only one H: the correct formula is CH≡CCH₂CH₃.

options: The molecule would have five carbon atoms
The first carbon would have five bonds
Hydrogen is not allowed in alkynes

questions.prompt: But-1-yne and but-2-yne both have the molecular formula
questions.explanation: Both are C₄H₆; they differ only in the position of the triple bond.

questions.prompt: Between which two carbon atoms is the triple bond in pent-1-yne?
questions.explanation: Starting on C-1 means between C-1 and C-2: CH≡CCH₂CH₂CH₃.

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are present in one molecule of pent-2-yne?
questions.explanation: Pent-2-yne: pent- = 5 carbons and -2-yne = a C≡C triple bond starting on C-2, so CH₃C≡CCH₂CH₃ (C₅H₈).

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are present in one molecule of but-2-yne?
questions.explanation: But-2-yne: but- = 4 carbons and -2-yne = a C≡C triple bond starting on C-2, so CH₃C≡CCH₃ (C₄H₆).

questions.prompt: What type of compound is hex-3-yne?
questions.explanation: Hex-3-yne: hex- = 6 carbons and -3-yne = a C≡C triple bond starting on C-3, so CH₃CH₂C≡CCH₂CH₃ (C₆H₁₀).

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are present in one molecule of hex-3-yne?
questions.explanation: Hex-3-yne: hex- = 6 carbons and -3-yne = a C≡C triple bond starting on C-3, so CH₃CH₂C≡CCH₂CH₃ (C₆H₁₀).

questions.prompt: CH₃CH₂CH=CHCH₃ is named pent-2-ene, not pent-3-ene, because
questions.explanation: From the right the double bond starts at C-2; from the left it starts at C-3; the rule is to choose the smaller number.

options: The double bond is in the middle of the chain
Numbering must always start from the CH₃ on the left
Numbering from the right gives the double bond the smaller number

questions.prompt: What does the number 2 in pent-2-ene indicate?
questions.explanation: It shows that the double bond starts on carbon 2 of the five-carbon chain.

options: The double bond starts on carbon number 2
There are two hydrogen atoms on carbon 5

questions.prompt: A compound whose name ends in “-ane” is
questions.explanation: Name endings: -ane alkane, -ene alkene, -yne alkyne, -ol alcohol, -oic acid carboxylic acid, -oate ester.

questions.prompt: A compound whose name ends in “-ene” is
questions.explanation: The ending -ene shows a C=C double bond.

questions.prompt: A compound whose name ends in “-yne” is
questions.explanation: The ending -yne shows a C≡C triple bond.

questions.prompt: A compound whose name ends in “-ol” is
questions.explanation: The ending -ol shows the –OH group.

questions.prompt: A compound whose name ends in “-oic acid” is
questions.explanation: The ending -oic acid shows the –COOH group.

questions.prompt: A compound whose name ends in “-oate” (with an alkyl word first) is
questions.explanation: Esters are named alkyl … -oate, e.g. methyl ethanoate.

questions.prompt: How can you recognise an ester from its formula?
questions.explanation: An ester has –COO– between two carbon groups.

options: It has the –COO– group between two carbon groups (RCOOR′)
It has only C–C single bonds
It has an –OH group on a carbon chain
It has a C≡C triple bond

questions.prompt: How can you recognise an alcohol from its formula?
questions.explanation: An alcohol is R–OH.

options: It has a C=C double bond
It has only C–C single bonds
It has a –COO– group between two chains
It has an –OH group attached to a carbon chain (R–OH)

questions.prompt: Can compounds with the same molecular formula belong to different families?
questions.explanation: C₃H₆O₂ can be propanoic acid (acid) or methyl ethanoate / ethyl methanoate (esters).

options: No, the molecular formula always decides the family
No, because every formula has only one structure
Yes, e.g. C₃H₆O₂ can be propanoic acid or an ester
Only if they are both alkanes

questions.prompt: The compound CH₃CH₂CH₃ is an alkane because
questions.explanation: No double bond, triple bond or functional group = alkane.

options: It has a C=C double bond
It has only C–C single bonds

questions.prompt: The compound CH₃CH₂OH is an alcohol because
questions.explanation: The –OH on a carbon chain makes it an alcohol (ethanol).

options: It has an –OH group on a carbon chain
It has a C=O group only

questions.prompt: The memory trick “Mice Eat Peanut Butter” helps you remember
questions.explanation: M-E-P-B = meth, eth, prop, but.

options: The stems meth, eth, prop and but

questions.prompt: The stems pent, hex, hept, oct, non and dec are the same as in the shapes
questions.explanation: Pentagon = 5 sides … decagon = 10 sides.

options: Pentagon, hexagon, heptagon, octagon, nonagon, decagon

questions.prompt: Which drawing recipe is correct (name → formula)?
questions.explanation: ① stem, ② suffix, ③ number and place the double bond / triple bond / –OH / –COOH, ④ add hydrogens.

options: Stem → suffix → number and place the group → add hydrogens to make four bonds on every carbon

questions.prompt: Which check should you do after drawing ANY formula?
questions.explanation: C = 4 lines, O = 2 lines, H = 1 line.

options: Check that the formula is symmetric
Check that it has an –OH group
Count four lines on every carbon
Count the vowels in the name

questions.prompt: A straight-chain hydrocarbon with at most one multiple bond has the molecular formula C₅H₁₂. Which family does it belong to?
questions.explanation: C₅H₁₂ with n = 5 fits CₙH₂ₙ₊₂: alkane.

questions.prompt: Which compound has the SAME molecular formula as propyl methanoate but a different structure?
questions.explanation: Propyl methanoate and butanoic acid are both C₄H₈O₂ but have different structures.

questions.prompt: Which compound has the SAME molecular formula as propanoic acid but a different structure?
questions.explanation: Propanoic acid and ethyl methanoate are both C₃H₆O₂ but have different structures.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH₂C≡CH?
questions.explanation: Number from the end that gives the smaller number: pent-1-yne, not pent-4-yne.

questions.prompt: How many C–C bonds are shown in the displayed formula of ethane?
questions.explanation: 2 carbons in a row are joined by 1 C–C bonds.

questions.prompt: How many C–H bonds are shown in the displayed formula of octane?
questions.explanation: Each hydrogen forms one C–H bond: 18 hydrogens = 18 C–H bonds.

questions.prompt: How many C–C bonds are shown in the displayed formula of heptane?
questions.explanation: 7 carbons in a row are joined by 6 C–C bonds.

questions.prompt: A straight-chain hydrocarbon with at most one multiple bond has the molecular formula C₄H₈. Which family does it belong to?
questions.explanation: C₄H₈ with n = 4 fits CₙH₂ₙ: alkene.

questions.prompt: How many C–H bonds are shown in the displayed formula of ethane?
questions.explanation: Each hydrogen forms one C–H bond: 6 hydrogens = 6 C–H bonds.

questions.prompt: A straight-chain hydrocarbon with at most one multiple bond has the molecular formula C₃H₆. Which family does it belong to?
questions.explanation: C₃H₆ with n = 3 fits CₙH₂ₙ: alkene.

questions.prompt: How many C–C bonds are shown in the displayed formula of hexane?
questions.explanation: 6 carbons in a row are joined by 5 C–C bonds.
